about: Vectors for the x402/exact/eip155/eip3009 pairing: the x402 and evm entry points of @integraledger/lcp. H is SHA-256("abc") from FIPS 180-2; O is the x402 specification's example option (section 5.2.1); the payer is the published Anvil development key. The EIP-712 values were computed with eth-account 0.14.0, eth-abi 6.0.0 and eth-utils 6.0.0 on Python 3.12.3; every SHA-256 with GNU coreutils sha256sum. The ERC-20 Transfer topic is keccak256("Transfer(address,address,uint256)"). Byte strings are hex; uint256 values are decimal strings. Under the profile read-status, a V6 row that would read failed (a revert, no use of H, no paired transfer) reads pending search-incomplete: its reader makes no log query, and at coverage full a failed answer waits for the search for H (rule 24).

V1.case: build({required: {x402Version: 2, resource, accepts: [O]}, accepted: O, from: payer, now}, H), then EIP-712

V2.case: complete(V1 signature), then bound. expectPayload is x402 v2's PaymentPayload, written by hand from the specification (x402-foundation/x402 751590a2, specs/x402-specification-v2.md §5.2.1-5.2.2, L152-213, and specs/schemes/exact/scheme_exact_evm.md §1, L24-63): x402Version 2, resource the fixed resource, accepted O, and payload {signature, authorization}, where signature is V1.expectSignature, computed with eth-account 0.14.0, and authorization is V1.expectMessage, the signed message in x402's string form. The PaymentRequired build is given carries no extensions, so the payload has none to echo.

conflict.case: advertise over a document whose legalContext carries another link

readHttpLink.case: read of the V5 document whose legalContextUrl is http://

readMalformed.case: read of the V5 document whose legalContext value is not a 32-byte hash

V6.about: Oracles: every AuthorizationUsed log is viem 2.57.4's encodeEventTopics of `event AuthorizationUsed(address indexed authorizer, bytes32 indexed nonce)` as EIP-3009 states it (https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3009, Events), with data "0x"; every Transfer log is viem's encodeEventTopics and encodeAbiParameters of viem's erc20Abi Transfer event (viem/_esm/constants/abis.js, erc20Abi); every transaction input is viem's encodeFunctionData of transferWithAuthorization(from, to, value, validAfter, validBefore, nonce, v, r, s) from @x402/evm 2.31.0's eip3009ABI (dist/esm/chunk-5AIYL4HT.mjs:83-99), the ABI the x402 facilitator settles with, alone or inside Multicall3's aggregate3 from viem's multicall3Abi, each signature viem's signTypedData by the published Anvil development key of its authorizer over V1's domain, with validAfter 0 and the ref's validBefore; the transferFrom call is viem's erc20Abi. A log whose topic 0 is 0x01, 0x02 or 0x03 (as a 32-byte word) is one no event of the token's ABI has, standing for another contract's event. The reader answers each row's receipt, the row's transaction where it carries one (null otherwise), the token's authorizationState(payer, H) as viem's encodeFunctionResult of eip3009ABI's authorizationState: true where the row's authorizationState is true (its receipt holds the payer's use of H on the asset), false otherwise, and no log query. test/vectors.test.ts decodes every such log and input with viem and re-encodes it to the same bytes, and recovers each signature to its authorizer.

notThisPayment.case: status of a named transaction that is not V2's payment: none settles V2's payment as presented. Another account's use of H is a foreign item, other-signer; the payer's use of H paying another value settles with presented "no"; a transfer with no use of H is no act. The pair one EIP-3009 authorization produces is its AuthorizationUsed(authorizer, nonce) and its Transfer(from = authorizer, to, value), in the token's code; the ref's transferLog digest is SHA-256 over payer, payTo and uint256(10000), from GNU coreutils sha256sum

rows.case: another account's own authorization with nonce H and its zero-value transfer to itself
another account's use of nonce H beside the payer's transfer of the same value to payTo
the payer's use of nonce H with a transfer of another value
the payer's transfer to payTo with no use of nonce H

pairing.case: status of a named transaction holding more than one AuthorizationUsed or transfer of the payer's. EIP-3009's reference implementation and Circle's FiatToken (USDC) emit AuthorizationUsed and then the transfer the authorization executes; ERC-3009 states no order. Where the authorizer has one use and at most one transfer on the token in the transaction, the two pair whatever their order. Otherwise the read decodes the transaction's input, takes the authorizer's one EIP-3009 call with that nonce, and pairs the use with a transfer of the authorizer's on the token, not already paired, of that call's value to that call's recipient; where the reader gives no transaction, or the input holds no such call or the logs no such transfer, the item holds the search. H2 is SHA-256("abd") and H3 SHA-256("abe") (GNU coreutils sha256sum); O is Anvil account 4, Q Anvil account 2, and the transaction's sender Anvil account 1. Each row's expect is exactEip3009.status's answer.

rows.name: secondSignature
rows.case: Multicall3's aggregate3 of two transferWithAuthorization calls of the payer's: H2's paying payTo 10000 and H's paying O 1 unit. The read decodes the transaction, takes the call whose nonce is H and pairs its use with the payer's transfer of that call's value to that call's recipient: 1 unit to O, so H's act names another account

rows.name: plainBeside
rows.case: Multicall3's aggregate3 of the token's transferFrom of 10000 from the payer to payTo and the payer's transferWithAuthorization with nonce H paying O 1 unit: two transfers of the payer's, so the read decodes the transaction and pairs H's use with the 1 unit to O

rows.name: batch
rows.case: Multicall3's aggregate3 of two payments of the payer's, H2's of 5000 and then H's of 10000, each use before its transfer as the token emits them: H's use pairs with the transfer its decoded call names, 10000 to payTo

rows.name: batchUnread
rows.case: batch's receipt where the reader gives no transaction: with two uses of the payer's on the token, the read cannot tell which transfer is H's, so the item holds the search

rows.name: transferFirst
rows.case: a token that emits the Transfer before AuthorizationUsed, with H's payment alone, called directly on the token: the payer's one use there pairs with its one transfer there, whatever their order

rows.name: transferFirstBatch
rows.case: a token that emits the Transfer first, in Multicall3's aggregate3 of H's payment and then the payer's H2 authorization of 1 unit to O: the read decodes the transaction and pairs H's use with the transfer its call names, 10000 to payTo

rows.name: transferFirstTwoPayers
rows.case: a token that emits the Transfer first, in Multicall3's aggregate3 of H's payment, Q's authorization with nonce H3 of 5 to O, and the payer's H2 authorization of 1 unit to O: the read decodes the payer's call with nonce H and pairs its use with the transfer it names

rows.name: oneUseOneTransfer
rows.case: logs in an order no token's single call emits: the payer's transfer of 10000 to payTo, Q's use of nonce H3, then the payer's use of H. The payer's one use on the token and its one transfer there pair whatever lies between them, since the read pairs by authorizer and token, not by order, and reads no transaction to do it

AG.case: The agreement's own value for H: SHA-256 over the 16 ASCII bytes `lcp-agreement-v1` (tagHex) followed by H's 32 bytes (preimageHex, 48 bytes), computed 2026-11-17 with GNU coreutils sha256sum and with openssl dgst -sha256 over those bytes, both giving expectValue; none was taken from the package's output. build(V1's choice, H, "agreement") signs V1's TransferWithAuthorization with nonce = expectValue; expectDigest is its EIP-712 digest, computed with viem 2.57.4's hashTypedData over V1's domain and EIP-3009's TransferWithAuthorization type (https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3009). bound of that payment answers expectValue with no act given, H given the act agreement and H, and x402/nonce-not-agreement for V2's payment, whose nonce is H, given the act agreement and H.

plant.case: a successful receipt whose only AuthorizationUsed log with topics[2] = H came from a contract other than the option's asset
plant.about: The plant's log is viem 2.57.4's encodeEventTopics of EIP-3009's AuthorizationUsed (https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3009, Events), from 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD; its reader gives no transaction, so the read cannot verify the authorization in that contract's own domain and holds the search.

MX.about: A challenge mixing an offer whose pairing is a public proof (x402/exact/eip155/eip3009) with one that is not (x402/exact/eip155/erc7710, the unsigned level; its option is x402-exact-eip155-erc7710.json's fixed option). The legal context is one per document: each offer's pairing advertises it with the agreement URL, in either order, and the document carries the URL once, after legalContextUrl. Either pairing's read returns it. A buyer paying through the public-proof pairing does not pay the agreement (buyer.json BA6).

agreedRefusals.about: Refusal codes where the pairing leaves the code to the implementation, as the TypeScript and Python implementations both apply them. A row that carries its input gives it: choice is build's choice, with H; info replaces V5's expectDocument's extensions.legalContext.info, legalContext its extensions.legalContext and accepts its accepts, for read; accepted replaces V1's option in build's choice, as the one entry of required.accepts and as accepted. A link's length is counted in UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript's String length counts it: each long link ends in U+10000, one code point of two UTF-16 code units, so it is 2049 UTF-16 code units and 2048 code points.

buyer.about: The buyer gate's rows for this file's pairings, in the form of buyer.json's rows. B2 is the plant: the document advertises H, the hash of the ATR in B6's first check, and the link serves the planted ATR, that ATR with one byte changed; the gate declines hash-mismatch and never calls the signer. B6 is the pairing's bound check over the payment this file already holds: check(ATR, presented) gives H, and check(planted ATR, presented) declines signed-not-bound. Where the ATR is abc, H is its SHA-256 (FIPS 180-2 B.1) and the planted ATR is abd. SHA-256 values are GNU coreutils sha256sum, which openssl dgst -sha256 matches. Bytes are hex. A B2 input names the account, the buyer's inputs and the time (now, in seconds) its build needs. noSignedPayment names each pairing of the file that has no B6 row, and why.
